text:
maria: heads up — canary from this morning (merge r/1725 + quant-profile flip) is showing a clear perf regression on short prompts. p95 gen latency jumped ~22% vs last good canary. small single-token throughput also down. :eyes:

perfbot: CI perf alert attached: perf/regression-int8: dequant wall-time increased (per-token) — see artifact https://artifacts.redwood/perf/1715009999 :rotating_light:

alex: thanks. I'm starting a local bisect across merges since 1714920000. initial hypothesis: the quant profile change in r/1725 that alters kernel selection weights.

jordan: telemetry snapshot from canary: KV cache hit rate dropped from ~98% -> ~86% for sequences < 64 tokens. batching shapes skewed smaller, so KV misses more expensive. also saw more frequent fallback to the slower int8_dequant_path kernel.

maria: repro steps I used: run the small prompt suite (10k samples) against canary. attach flamegraph snippet below:

```
# top stack samples
dequant::apply 1834 samples (was 720)
kv_cache::lookup 620 samples (was 450)
kernel_selector::choose 310 samples
attention::matmul_int8 210 samples
```

alex: interesting — kernel_selector is picking `int8_avx_generic` for several layers now instead of `int8_fast_kv` because of the new policy that prefers lower memory footprint. that policy change was part of the quant-profile flip.

sam: can we pin the model to the previous quant profile for the canary while we bisect? `redwoodctl models pin --model my-model --profile quant-v1` should do it. If pin fixes perf, we can rollback the profile change.

lee: I've paused the dark launch and set traffic to 0% for the canary. also opened a small PR to revert the quant-profile flip: https://git/repo/pulls/1789 — tagging for fast review.

alex: bisect progress: tested merges r/1720..r/1728. isolate shows regression introduced in r/1725 (quant-profile: prefer-memory-saver). The exact diff is the kernel preference weights and a new heuristic for short sequences.

jordan: side note: quality metrics are roughly flat (perplexity and eval prompts unchanged) so it's a pure perf tradeoff. worth deciding: keep memory-optimized kernels or prioritize latency for low-latency routes.

maria: agree. for prod-hosted low-latency route we should prefer the faster kernel even if it uses slightly more working set. can we add a per-route override?

alex: yeah we can. quick patch: add `kernel_policy: preferred_kernels: [int8_fast_kv, int8_avx_generic]` to route config. I'll draft a canary-only override so Dedicated/Private unaffected.

oncall: FYI I announced an incident note to #incidents for visibility. rolling rollback in progress: lee's PR merged and rollback job started at 1715010200.

perfbot: rollback job logs: 
- triggered revert r/1725 -> r/1725-revert-1789
- canary traffic switch -> 0% at 1715010305
- new canary build promoted at 1715010400
- perf snapshot at 1715010500 shows p95 back within 2% of baseline

maria: great, looks like revert fixes it. next actions:
- alex, make a follow-up that exposes per-route kernel preferences and documents the perf/memory tradeoff.
- jordan, add a short-term telemetry alert for KV hit-rate drop > 5% for short prompts.
- sam, improve `redwoodctl` to pin quant profile by route.

sam: noted, will send quick PR for pin-by-route CLI.

lee: leaving the rollback in place and will coordinate with infra to re-run the quant-profile tests in a staging matrix (vary seq-len, batch size, kv-hit scenarios).

maria: thanks all. Filing a postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have the perf artifacts and the staging matrix results. good job catching this early. :thumbsup:
